what: Every human decision that shapes the generated community catalog. bots.json is the scrape and is never edited; this file is where a person's judgement lives, each row carrying the exact string it replaces and why. scripts/build-bot-catalog.mjs FAILS when a `from` is no longer found, so a row cannot rot quietly against a future re-scrape.
order: The vendor phrase table in the generator runs FIRST; every `from` below is matched against the text as it stands AFTER that table. That is why some rows read as if the rename had already happened.

drop.why: Its whole job is packaging and publishing plugins into the old vendor's plugin directory. Renaming the vendor out of it leaves skills and memories describing a publishing pipeline this product does not have, which is a broken bot wearing our name.
Its job is designing and creating more of the old vendor's bots through their own create-a-bot call, and auditing a fleet of them. Nothing under it survives the rename.
Its method is shelling out to a signed-in vendor CLI on the machine, pinned to a vendor model. Without that binary it is a research desk with no way to research, and we already ship one that works.
It governs a fleet of the old vendor's bots: its memories are an operating model for their org, their skills and their routines. There is no honest rename of that.

category.why: The scrape gives it no category at all. It watches public channels for mentions of your company and competitors and hands the ones worth a reply to a seller, so Sales is where a person would look for it.
The scrape gives it no category at all. It runs a household: school pickups, the family digest, the kitchen newspaper. Personal is the only chip it belongs under.
Its only scraped category was the team grouping we drop. It works the vendor contract list, renewals and spend, which is the operations desk's job.

replace.why: A watch list of AI companies that happens to name the old upstream. The list is the operator's to edit on day one, and one name out of five costs nothing; keeping it would put that vendor's name on a page a customer reads.

replace.to: There is no Bland row in this Marketplace yet, so add it yourself as a custom server.
replace.why: The phrase table turns the vendor's marketplace into ours, which then reads as a flat refusal. The true sentence names the door that does exist.

replace.from: Register it as a Titanium Bot skill. Do not install it as a marketplace plugin.
replace.to: Register it as a skill on this bot. Do not install it as a marketplace plugin.
replace.why: "a Titanium Bot skill" is the phrase table being literal; a skill belongs to the bot, and that is what the sentence should say.

replace.from: Grok CLI (`grok login --device-auth`) is a valid X path when available; pin LAST30DAYS_X_BACKEND=grok.
replace.why: The sentence is machinery this product does not have: a signed-in vendor CLI on the box. The two honest paths (sign in on this computer, or skip X) are stated in the sentence before it, so removing this one loses nothing.

replace.from: or they provide an xAI/Xquik key, or skip X.
replace.to: or they provide an Xquik key, or skip X.
replace.why: Names the old vendor as a key source. Xquik is the third-party path and stays.

replace.from: launch a cloud coding agent (Fable 5) into the sticky demo monorepo
replace.to: launch a cloud coding agent into the sticky demo monorepo
replace.why: The phrase table already replaced the vendor's product name; the model in brackets was theirs to pin and is not ours to promise.

schedule.note: Every hour at :35, weekdays, the cadence this routine states.
schedule.why: The only routine in the pack whose cadence is an intra-day minute mark rather than a daily hour. Read from its own summary, "refresh at :35 (catch at :40)"; the generator's hour rules would have quietly turned an hourly job into a 9am one.

schedule.note: Weekdays at 3:15 PM, the cadence this routine states.
schedule.why: "ship at 3:15 local" with no am or pm. It is a cash close, so it is the afternoon; written down here rather than guessed by the generator, which requires am or pm before it reads a clock.
